newsitem.title: PANAMA: Venezuelan chopper may have lost fuel before crash.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan chopper may have lost fuel before crash.

text.p: A small Venezuelan-owned helicopter may have lost fuel before crashing near a Panama City cemetery on Saturday leaving its three passengers seriously injured, according to the daily newspaper El Panama America published Sunday.

Civil Air Service officials were investigating reports that the Huey 500 helicopter, owned by the Venezuelan tuna fishing company Oriental Prestige Marine, lost fuel 20 minutes after takeoff from the national Paitilla Airport in Panama City, the newspaper reported.
The helicopter was on a test run before it crashed near the Jardin de Paz cemetery in Panama City, according to the newspaper.
The pilot and two passengers were taken to the private Paitilla Hospital where their condition was upgraded from critical to serious condition, the newspaper reported.
Witnesses told the newspaper they saw the passengers jump from the chopper shortly before it crashed. But those reports were later denied by Civil Air Service officials, the newspaper said.
A Civil Air Service spokesman said the destination or nationality of the passengers were not immediately known. The crash occurred in clear weather and the chopper was destroyed, he said.
